A_target.statement:
Let $S$ be a set and $A, B \subseteq S$.
Then:
:$\relcomp S {A \cup B} = \relcomp S A \cap \relcomp S B$
:$\relcomp S {A \cap B} = \relcomp S A \cup \relcomp S B$

B_source.statement:
Let $S$ be a set.
Then [[Definition:Relative Complement|complementation]] $A \mapsto \relcomp S A$ on the [[Definition:Power Set|power set]] $\powerset S$ satisfies:
:$A \subseteq B \iff \relcomp S B \subseteq \relcomp S A$
:$\relcomp S {\relcomp S A} = A$

derived.the second De Morgan law: the image of the first under the involution

validity_conditions: complementation must be an involution, so applying it twice returns the original set
it must reverse inclusion, which is what exchanges least upper bounds with greatest lower bounds
the ambient universe must be fixed, since complement is taken relative to it
proof_plan:
From [[Set Complement inverts Subsets]], complementation reverses inclusion.
From [[Relative Complement of Relative Complement]], it is an [[Definition:Involution (Mapping)|involution]], hence a [[Definition:Bijection|bijection]].
An [[Definition:Order-Reversing Mapping|order-reversing]] bijection with order-reversing inverse carries [[Definition:Supremum of Set|suprema]] to [[Definition:Infimum of Set|infima]].

In $\struct {\powerset S, \subseteq}$, $A \cup B = \sup \set {A, B}$ and $A \cap B = \inf \set {A, B}$.
Hence:
:$\relcomp S {A \cup B} = \relcomp S A \cap \relcomp S B$

Apply this identity to $\relcomp S A$ and $\relcomp S B$, then complement:
:$\relcomp S {A \cap B} = \relcomp S A \cup \relcomp S B$

The argument used only the [[Definition:Lattice|lattice]] structure and the complement, so it holds in any [[Definition:Boolean Algebra|Boolean algebra]].
{{qed}}
